calls.title: Nodir Nasirov and Cary Rakin
calls.summary: The discussion centered on the restructuring at Conde and its impact on managing Growth Book. Cary Rakin introduced himself, acknowledging Mark's departure and expressing readiness to assist Nodir Nasirov in his evolving role. Nodir, who has led Growth Book deployment for about four to five years, is now responsible for maintaining the self-hosted platform after team cuts. Cary emphasized the importance of proactive support and the potential benefits of cloud hosting, including quicker issue resolution. They analyzed initial cost comparisons between self-hosting and cloud options, projecting user growth that necessitates scalable pricing solutions. Further discussions on technical considerations revealed billing uncertainties that need addressing, while strategic plans for cloud hosting pivot around balancing operational efficiency and cost.
calls.keywords: Growth Book, Cloud Hosting, Self-Hosted, Proxy Requests, Experimentation, AI Integration
calls.action_items:
**Nodir Nasirov**
Forward the two Growth Book contract quotes Cary sent to Mark to Nodir's manager and explain the cost implications of cloud hosting (12:36)
Provide detailed data on proxy request volumes to Growth Book team for further pricing evaluation (20:26)

**Cary Rakin**
Send Nodir the two existing contract quotes previously sent to Mark for internal review (12:38)
Confirm with Growth Book team whether proxy API requests from Growth Proxy will incur additional charges or be covered under platform fees (16:51)
Arrange a technical call between Growth Book engineers and Conde Nast team to review proxy request impact and AI system integration for experiment automation (22:09)
Provide updated pricing quotes based on user growth and proxy request considerations before formal contract submission (25:50)
